# P675: JS engine for the API MCP

Planner: Opus. Implementer: one sequential Sonnet subagent. No streams: one new package, one
`go.mod` change, one argv-shim line, order-dependent.

Spec row: embedded JavaScript engine in Go for the API MCP (P676 to P679) and DB MCP (P680), never
UI-facing. Hard CPU limit and interrupt, memory ceiling, output cap, no filesystem, network,
process, timers or `require`, deterministic globals, big-integer handling documented, structured
errors with line and column, one package with a narrow interface. Not in scope: jq or gojq.

Rewritten for `github.com/dop251/goja` (user decision: most popular and maintained pure-Go engine).
This replaces the modernc QuickJS plan of commit `5cfa1b274`. Engine-neutral design (interface,
script shape, source checks, error shape, big-integer rules, tests, docs) carries over; what goja
forces is new: a worker subprocess for the ceilings, Go-side guards, goja error mapping.

## Discovery (codegraph)

- No JS engine or script sandbox exists. `internal/scripts` and `internal/scriptruns` run shell
  processes; `internal/agentsandbox` renders a macOS Seatbelt profile for agent CLIs.
- `dbmcp/api_tools.go`: `apiRequest` plans, approves (`approveAPI`), then `Send` returns a masked,
  capped `agentapi.Result` as JSON. P676 inserts the engine between `Send` and `jsonResult`; P675
  touches neither.
- Approval-binding precedent: `scriptruns.PlanMCP` returns `Preview.Hash`; `StartMCP` refuses a
  changed script (`checkStart`). The engine's source hash follows that shape.
- Worker-process precedent: `appwire.RunArgvShim` dispatches hidden subcommands of the app binary
  (`askpass`, `memory-mcp`, `memory-ingest`, `memory-embed`, `memory-check`) before Wails starts.
  `memembed.Client` spawns `executable() memory-embed` "so a native crash cannot take the host
  down", over NDJSON on stdin/stdout through `internal/memory/workerproc` (pipes, hello under a
  timeout, `Kill`, `Stop`, stderr tail). `memembed` tests re-exec the test binary from `TestMain`.
  `flowharness` main also calls `RunArgvShim`, so P676 flow tests get the worker for free.
- No in-app heap watchdog exists. `internal/metrics` samples process RSS with
  `shirou/gopsutil/v4/process` (already a dependency).
- `dbmcp/browse.go` and `oplog/redact.go` decode JSON with `UseNumber`; `internal/jsonx` keeps
  object key order.
- Packaging (`docs/PACKAGING.md`): macOS arm64 only, `CGO_ENABLED=1` (Wails). Dev and CI run
  linux/amd64. goja is pure Go, so the darwin target cross-builds here with `CGO_ENABLED=0`.

## Decision: `github.com/dop251/goja`, run in a worker process

goja runs scripts. Each `Exec` runs in a fresh `kira-space js-worker` child process (the app binary
re-executed, as `memory-embed` is). In-process goja cannot hold the memory ceiling or the CPU limit;
the probes below show single calls and operators that kill the whole process or never return.

### Candidates

- `github.com/dop251/goja` (chosen). Commit `8dfece3d1e1d717c1bfdc9be25186a7be06a5f12`,
  2026-11-18, pseudo-version `v0.0.0-20261118204651-8dfece3d1e1d`, `go 1.26.0` (repo is 1.27.3).
  MIT. About 7.2k stars, active commits, one main maintainer (Dmitry Panov). ES2022 works
  (optional chaining, private fields, BigInt, spread, `.at()`, `findLast`, `toSorted`, `with`,
  `Float16Array`). No async generators ("Async generators are not supported yet", syntax error).
  Runtime hooks: `Interrupt`/`ClearInterrupt`, `SetMaxCallStackSize`, `SetRandSource`,
  `SetTimeSource`, `SetParserOptions`. No memory limit API; `Interrupt` does not reach native
  built-ins (its own doc says so).
- `modernc.org/quickjs` v0.27.0: previous choice (real allocator limit, interrupt polled inside
  regexp and sort). Dropped by user decision on popularity and maintainer base.
- `github.com/grafana/sobek`: goja fork for k6, same core and same gaps. `fastschema/qjs` (QuickJS
  on wazero): pre-1.0, no release for a year. `buke/quickjs-go`, `v8go`: cgo, darwin cgo cannot be
  built or vetted here. `otto`: ES5, no limits. All rejected.

### Probes (goja at the commit above, linux/amd64, scratch module, 1 GB heap watchdog)

Single built-in calls, in-process, `Interrupt` armed at 500 ms (interrupt lands only after the call
returns):

| Call | Wall | Heap peak |
|---|---|---|
| `'x'.repeat(2**27)`, `padStart`, `padEnd` | 340-400 ms | +128 MB |
| `''.concat(...Array(128).fill(1 MiB string))` | 543 ms | +129 MB |
| `Array(128).fill(1 MiB string).join('')` | 997 ms | +334 MB |
| `Array(2**27).join('x')` (sparse) | 10.4 s | +437 MB |
| `Array(2**24).fill(0)` | killed | > 975 MB |
| `Array.from({length:2**23})` | 2.2 s | +421 MB |
| `a.flat(Infinity)`, `a` = 2^22 shared-node DAG | 1.5 s | +215 MB |
| `String(a)`, 2^24 DAG (toString via `join`) | 9.3 s | +103 MB |
| `JSON.stringify(a)`, 2^24 DAG | 9.0 s | +374 MB |
| `'x'.repeat(2**22).split('')` | 247 ms | +195 MB |
| `new Float64Array(2**25)` | 0 ms | +256 MB |
| `JSON.parse` of 8 MiB `[{"a":1},...]` | 1.25 s | +607 MB |
| `replaceAll` / `replace(/a/g)` of 4 Ki chars with a 32 Ki string | 2 s | +434 MB |
| `Math.max.apply(null,{length:2**24})`, `Reflect.apply`, `String.fromCharCode.apply` | 1.2 s | +383-415 MB |
| `2n**(2n**30n)` | 2.7 s | +640 MB |
| `Array(2**24)` then `map` / `sort` / `[...a]` | 1-2 s | +383-512 MB |
| `Array(2**31).forEach(f)` (holes, no callback) | > 30 s, never interrupted | flat |
| `/^(a+)+$/.test('a'.repeat(32)+'b')` | > 60 s, never interrupted | flat |
| `'x'.repeat(2**25)` matched by `/y/` | 327 ms | +160 MB (regexp2 copies to `[]rune`) |

Process killers in-process (unrecoverable Go `fatal error`, whole app dies):

- Rope flatten. goja concatenates lazily: `s=s+s` 60 times builds a 2^60-length rope in 0.1 ms. Any
  `===`, template literal or property-key use flattens it in one native copy (2^28: +256-512 MB in
  250-720 ms; 2^36: `fatal error: runtime: out of memory`). Operators cannot be wrapped.
- `BigInt.asUintN(2**40, -1n)`: `fatal error: runtime: out of memory` at once.
- Deep nesting, native recursion: `JSON.parse('['.repeat(3e5)+...)`, `a.flat(Infinity)`,
  `String(a)` on `a=[a]` x 3e5: `fatal error: stack overflow` (Go stack, probe capped at 64 MiB;
  default 1 GiB cap only delays it).

What works in-process: `SetMaxCallStackSize(10000)` turns JS recursion into
`*goja.StackOverflowError` in 24 ms; plain JS loops interrupt on time; a comparator loop inside
`sort` interrupts (JS callback); `regexp2.DefaultMatchTimeout` (package var, read at regexp compile)
turns the catastrophic regexp into a catchable `RangeError: match timeout after 250ms` (402 ms);
goja's parser caps nesting ("Maximum nesting depth exceeded") so compile is safe in-process;
`goja.New` + tiny run costs 4.4 µs.

In-process heap watchdog (question a), sampling `/memory/classes/heap/objects:bytes` every 10 ms,
64 MiB budget over a baseline, forced `runtime.GC()` and recheck before interrupting all active
VMs:

- No ballast: push loop interrupted at 141 ms (+72 MB), string array at 893 ms (+85 MB), garbage
  churn not tripped over 2 s (1 forced GC). With 400 MB live ballast: push loop +160 MB (2.5x
  budget: the script keeps allocating while the forced GC runs), churn caused 16 forced GCs in 2 s
  (115 ms of GC work on the app's heap).
- Concurrent churn plus push loop: both interrupted; no per-goroutine allocation accounting in Go,
  so an innocent run dies with the guilty one.
- Holds for accumulation in JS code; cannot stop any single native call or operator above, and
  cannot prevent the three fatal paths.

Worker probe (question h): child process per script, `debug.SetMemoryLimit(128 MiB)`,
`debug.SetMaxStack(64 MiB)`, watchdog every 5 ms (soft: heap objects over baseline, forced GC,
`Interrupt`; hard: `/memory/classes/total:bytes` over 224 MiB, `os.Exit(75)`), env only
`GOTRACEBACK=none GOMAXPROCS=2 TZ=UTC`, parent kill at timeout + 1 s:

| Script | Wall | Exit | Child max RSS | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| garbage churn | 2003 ms | 0 | 14 MB | timeout, positioned, no false memory trip |
| push loop | 547 ms | 0 | 168 MB | `memory at <eval>:1:29`, positioned |
| `'x'.repeat(2**29)` | 9 ms | 75 | 11 MB | hard exit (heap accounted at allocation, before the copy) |
| rope 2^29 `===` | 8 ms | 75 | 13 MB | hard exit |
| rope 2^36 `===` | 6 ms | 2 | 8 MB | Go out of memory, child only |
| `BigInt.asUintN(2**40,-1n)` | 7 ms | 2 | 8 MB | Go out of memory, child only |
| deep `JSON.parse` | 177 ms | 2 | 131 MB | `goroutine stack exceeds 67108864-byte limit` |
| sparse `forEach` 2^31 | 3001 ms | killed | 14 MB | parent kill at deadline + grace |
| `2n**(2n**30n)` | 457 ms | 75 | 149 MB | hard exit |

Spawn, run `[1,2,3].map(...)`, exit: 3.4 ms average (10.7 MB probe binary, linux). The app binary
is larger and runs every package `init`; implementer measures it (below).

### Subprocess or in-process (question h)

Recommendation: worker subprocess, one run per process. Tradeoff:

- For: the app survives every probe; memory and CPU ceilings become hard (kill), not approximate;
  per-run memory attribution is exact (one script per process), so no innocent-run kills and no
  forced GC on the app heap; process globals become safe per run (`regexp2.DefaultMatchTimeout`,
  `time.Local`, `debug.SetMemoryLimit`, `debug.SetMaxStack`); a runaway built-in no longer holds a
  goroutine and a slot forever (old Known open item gone).
- Against: a few ms per run (spawn and package init); host calls cross a pipe (NDJSON round trip,
  tens of µs); more moving parts (protocol, exit-code mapping); worst-case memory is per process.
- The `Run`/`HostFunc` interface is already JSON in, JSON out, so nothing outside the package sees
  the process boundary.

## Package

`apps/kira-space/internal/jsengine`. Imports stdlib, goja (`goja`, `goja/parser`),
`dlclark/regexp2/v2` (match timeout only), `gopsutil/v4/process` (child RSS) and
`internal/memory/workerproc`. Never imports `bridge`, `dbmcp`, `agentapi`, `secrets`. P675 ships the
package, its tests and the argv-shim line; P676 wires the first caller. An exported package
without a production caller is by design for this phase.

Files:

- `engine.go`: `Engine`, `New`, `Exec`: validation, input encoding, semaphore, spawn, protocol
  loop, host-call dispatch, deadline, cancel, RSS watch, exit mapping.
- `worker.go`: `RunWorker(args []string) int`: read one request, set process limits, build VM, run,
  encode, reply, exit.
- `watchdog.go`: in-worker soft and hard memory watchdog.
- `limits.go`: `Limits`, defaults, ceilings, `normalize`.
- `source.go`: `SourceHash`, `Check`, source validation, wrapper.
- `sandbox.go`: global removal, dynamic-code block, clock, PRNG, freeze driver.
- `guards.go`: size-checked wrappers of allocating built-ins (guard list below).
- `json.go`: JSON to goja values (lossless big integers, depth cap), counting replacer, output
  marker restore.
- `bindings.go`: `Binding`, `HostFunc`, name rules, host-call trampoline (worker side) and
  dispatcher (parent side) with panic recovery.
- `errors.go`: `Error`, `Kind`, mapping from goja errors and worker exits, frame scrub.
- `protocol.go`: NDJSON message types.
- `freeze.js` (`//go:embed`): cycle-safe deep freeze walk, run once per VM. Function names start
  `__kira_` so frame scrubbing drops them.
- `apps/kira-space/internal/appwire/wire.go`: one `case "js-worker": return
  jsengine.RunWorker(args[2:]), true` in `RunArgvShim`, and its doc line.

### Interface

```go
// Engine runs scripts. Safe for concurrent use; each Exec runs in its own worker process.
type Engine struct{ /* sem chan struct{}; command func() *exec.Cmd */ }

func New() *Engine // MaxConcurrent slots; worker = os.Executable() (symlinks resolved) + "js-worker"

type Run struct {
	Source   string
	Bindings []Binding
	Limits   Limits    // zero fields take defaults
	Now      time.Time // Date.now() and new Date() for the whole run; zero = time.Now() at Exec start
	Seed     uint64    // Math.random seed; 0 = derived from SourceHash
}

type Binding struct {
	Name  string              // global identifier the script reads
	Value json.RawMessage     // eager JSON value; or
	Funcs map[string]HostFunc // an object of host methods (Value nil)
}

// HostFunc gets the JS call's arguments as one JSON array (lossless big integers) and returns one
// JSON value. A returned error throws Error(err.Error()) in the script; a panic is recovered.
// Runs in the app process, called over the worker pipe.
type HostFunc func(ctx context.Context, args json.RawMessage) (json.RawMessage, error)

type Result struct {
	JSON    json.RawMessage // compact, key order as JSON.stringify gives it, big integers exact; "null" for undefined
	Type    string          // undefined | null | boolean | number | bigint | string | array | object
	Elapsed time.Duration   // script time inside the worker, spawn excluded
}

func (e *Engine) Exec(ctx context.Context, r Run) (Result, error) // error is *Error, or an internal fault
func SourceHash(source string) string                             // hex sha256 of the exact bytes
func Check(source string) *Error                                  // validation + compile only, never runs
func RunWorker(args []string) int                                 // js-worker subcommand body
```

Nothing else exported except `Kind` constants, `Error`, `Frame`, `Limits` and the limit constants.
Test seam: unexported `newEngine(command func() *exec.Cmd)`; package tests re-exec the test binary
(`TestMain` runs `RunWorker` when `os.Args[1] == "js-worker"`, as `memembed` does). P676 to P680
extend through `Bindings` and `Limits`, never new entry points, unless a later plan proves the need.

### Script shape

- Source is a function body. Wrapper `(function () {"use strict";\n` + source + `\n})`, compiled
  with `parser.ParseFile(..., parser.WithDisableSourceMaps)` and `goja.CompileAST(prg, true)`, run,
  and the resulting function called from Go (`goja.AssertFunction`) with `this` undefined. The
  script ends with `return <value>`. Lines report as line − 1; columns unchanged. `Check` uses the
  same wrapper and parse, so a syntax error reads the same in `Check` and `Exec`.
- Breaking out of the wrapper (`}); ...; (function(){`) only runs more code in the same sandbox;
  accepted. A test pins that it gains nothing.
- Bindings are read-only globals (`DefineDataProperty`, not writable, not configurable, not
  enumerable). Name rule `^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,31}$`, not a reserved word, not an existing global,
  not `kira`, unique per run. Binding values are not frozen (per-run, mutation harmless).
- Built-in helper object `kira` (frozen): `kira.parseJSON(text)`, lossless (below). Only helper in
  P675; later phases add theirs as `Bindings`, not in the sandbox.
- Returning a Promise or thenable: `KindOutput`, "script returned a Promise; return a plain value".
  goja runs promise jobs when the stack empties; with no timers or I/O nothing settles from
  outside, and the worker exits after the reply. Top-level `await` is a syntax error in a non-async
  body; `import()` is a syntax error in goja ("Unexpected reserved word", probe).

### Limits

| Field | Default | Ceiling | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Timeout` (wall clock, whole run) | 2 s | 10 s | worker: `Interrupt` at deadline (positioned `KindTimeout`); regexp match timeout; parent: kill at deadline + 1 s grace |
| `MemoryBytes` | 256 MiB | 1 GiB | worker: `debug.SetMemoryLimit`, soft watchdog interrupt, hard exit; parent: RSS kill |
| `InputBytes` (sum of binding JSON) | 4 MiB | 32 MiB | parent before spawn; per host-call args and return; per `kira.parseJSON` text |
| `OutputBytes` | 1 MiB | 8 MiB | counting replacer in worker; parent checks bytes again |
| Source | 64 KiB | fixed | `Check`/`Exec` validation |
| JSON nesting depth (input, host calls, `kira.parseJSON`, `JSON.parse`) | 256 | fixed | Go token scanner |
| Host calls per run | 10,000 | fixed | trampoline counter |
| JS call stack | 10,000 frames | fixed | `SetMaxCallStackSize` |
| Go stack (native recursion) | 64 MiB | fixed | `debug.SetMaxStack` in worker |
| Concurrent runs | 4 | fixed | `Engine` semaphore, one worker per slot |

- Zero field: default. Above ceiling: `Exec` returns an internal error (programming error). No
  silent clamp.
- Memory sizing: object-dense JSON costs about 22x its text in goja's heap (probe: 3.5 MB text,
  75 MB retained). `Exec` refuses with `KindInput` when total input bytes × 24 > `MemoryBytes`
  ("input too large for the memory limit; raise MemoryBytes"). Defaults leave about 2x headroom.
- "CPU limit": Go has no per-goroutine CPU clock; the wall-clock deadline bounds CPU for a
  single-threaded VM, and the parent kill makes it hard. Say so in ARCHITECTURE.
- Worst-case engine memory: 4 × hard ceiling (`MemoryBytes` × 5/4 + 64 MiB, below), about 1.5 GiB
  at defaults, 5.3 GiB at ceilings, all in child processes, plus parent-side copies of input and
  output.

### Worker process and protocol

- Spawn: `exec.Cmd` from `command()`, `cmd.Env = ["GOTRACEBACK=none", "GOMAXPROCS=2", "TZ=UTC"]`
  only (no inherited environment: no tokens, no `HOME`), `cmd.Dir = os.TempDir()`, started with
  `workerproc.Start`. `GOTRACEBACK=none` keeps a fatal error to its header lines, so the 2 KiB
  stderr tail holds them.
- NDJSON on stdin/stdout, types in `protocol.go`:
  1. worker → `{"ready":true}` (`workerproc.Hello`, 10 s timeout, ctx honoured).
  2. parent → one request: source, bindings (`value` raw JSON, or `funcs` names), normalized
     limits, now (ms), seed.
  3. worker → zero or more `{"call":{"id","binding","fn","args"}}`; parent answers each with
     `{"reply":{"id","result"}}` or `{"reply":{"id","error"}}`. One call in flight (the VM blocks).
  4. worker → final `{"result":{"json","type","elapsedNs"}}` or `{"error":<Error>}`, then exits 0.
- Parent loop: reads lines in a goroutine; selects on lines, ctx done, deadline + 1 s, RSS-watch
  trip and process exit. Any kill path calls `Proc.Kill` and waits for `Done`. The semaphore slot
  is released after the process has exited, never before.
- Parent RSS watch: every 50 ms `process.NewProcess(pid).MemoryInfo().RSS`; above hard ceiling +
  64 MiB: kill, `KindMemory`. Backstop only; the worker's own watchdog normally acts first.
- Worker, before building the VM: `debug.SetMemoryLimit(MemoryBytes)`, `debug.SetMaxStack(64 MiB)`,
  `time.Local = time.UTC`, `regexp2.DefaultMatchTimeout = Timeout`, start the watchdog after input
  values are built (baseline = heap objects then).
- Watchdog (`watchdog.go`), every 5 ms, `runtime/metrics`:
  - soft: `/memory/classes/heap/objects:bytes` − baseline > `MemoryBytes` → `runtime.GC()` (at most
    every 50 ms), reread, still over → `vm.Interrupt(interruptMemory)`. Uncatchable in the script
    (probe: `*goja.InterruptedError` escapes `try`). Positioned `KindMemory`.
  - hard: `/memory/classes/total:bytes` > `MemoryBytes` × 5/4 + 64 MiB → `os.Exit(75)`. A large
    allocation is accounted before its copy runs, so the exit lands within one tick (probe: 6-9 ms,
    child RSS 8-13 MB).
  - Host-call waits select on the deadline too, so a stuck `HostFunc` cannot hold the worker past
    it.
- Exit mapping in parent when no final line arrived: exit 75 → `KindMemory`; stderr contains
  `out of memory` → `KindMemory`; `stack exceeds` or `stack overflow` → `KindStack`; killed at
  deadline → `KindTimeout`; killed on ctx → `KindCanceled`; RSS kill → `KindMemory`; anything else
  → `KindInternal`. These carry no line or column. Message is fixed text per kind; the stderr tail
  is never returned or logged (a Go panic value could carry data); log exit code only.
- Measure in Result: average `Exec` of a trivial script through the real app binary (dev build,
  linux), and through the test binary.

### Sandbox: globals

`goja.New()`; never `require`/`goja_nodejs`, never `console`, never `SetFieldNameMapper` or Go
object exposure (bindings enter as plain JS values built from JSON). Probe confirms `typeof` is
`undefined` for `require`, `process`, `console`, `print`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval`,
`queueMicrotask`, `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `WebAssembly`, `performance`, `WeakRef`,
`FinalizationRegistry`, `Atomics`, `SharedArrayBuffer`, `Intl`, `structuredClone`. Setup, in
order, in Go:

1. `SetParserOptions(parser.WithDisableSourceMaps)` and the same option on `Check`/`Exec` parse.
   Why: goja's default source-map loader calls `os.ReadFile` on a `//# sourceMappingURL=` path from
   the script (`parser/statement.go`), a filesystem read.
2. `SetMaxCallStackSize(10000)`; `SetTimeSource(func() time.Time { return now })` (fixed for the
   run); `SetRandSource` from `math/rand/v2` PCG seeded with `Run.Seed` (default: first 8 bytes of
   `SourceHash`). `time.Local = time.UTC` in the worker makes every local-time method UTC
   (probe with `TZ=America/New_York`: `getTimezoneOffset()` 0, `getHours()` 0, `toString()` ends
   `GMT+0000 (UTC)`). No Date subclass.
3. Delete `eval`. Dynamic code off: replace `Function` and the `constructor` of
   `Function.prototype` and of the async and generator function prototypes with a Go thrower
   (`EvalError: dynamic code is disabled`) whose `prototype` is the original, so `instanceof
   Function` works. goja has no async generators, so there is no fourth prototype. Probe: `Function`,
   `(function(){}).constructor`, async and generator constructors, `Reflect.construct(Function,…)`
   all throw; indirect `eval` is gone. Why: the approval card shows the script; code built from
   data at run time (for example from an API response carrying injected text) would run logic the
   user never saw.
4. Guards (`guards.go`, list below) installed over the originals.
5. `BigInt.prototype.toJSON`: Go function; returns `marker + digits` while the output encoder runs
   (run-state flag), else `this.toString()`. So `JSON.stringify` inside a script gives a digit
   string, not goja's "Do not know how to serialize a BigInt", and the encoder still sees every
   bigint. A replacer alone cannot do this: `toJSON` runs before the replacer (ECMA-262
   SerializeJSONProperty).
6. Define `kira`, install bindings, run `freeze.js`: every global intrinsic, its `prototype`, their
   own property values that are objects or functions (cycle-safe, `Set`), then
   `Object.freeze(globalThis)`. Strict mode makes writes throw (probe: "Cannot add property x,
   object is not extensible").

### Guards (question b)

Purpose: turn the common single-call blow-ups into a positioned, catchable `RangeError` before
anything is allocated. The worker ceilings stay the safety net; guards are for clear errors.
`callCap = MemoryBytes / 4` bytes per call; strings count 2 bytes per code unit (goja rope `.length`
is O(1), so lengths read without flattening); array slots count 16 bytes. A guard error is a
`RangeError` whose message starts `memory limit:` and names the built-in; run state keeps the
thrown object, and if it is the uncaught exception the run ends `KindMemory` with its position.
Each guard is a Go function replacing the property (same `name`, `length`, non-enumerable), which
calls the captured original after the check.

| # | Built-ins | Check before calling the original | Probe it answers |
|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | `String.prototype.repeat`, `padStart`, `padEnd`, `concat` | result length from `this.length` and args ≤ callCap | repeat/pad 128 MB, concat 129 MB |
| G2 | `Array.prototype.join` (also reached by `toString`, which looks `join` up) | (len − 1) × sep + Σ string element lengths + 24 per non-string primitive ≤ callCap; length ≤ 2^24; recursion depth (join inside join) ≤ 256 | join 334-437 MB, toString DAG, deep toString stack overflow |
| G3 | `Array.prototype` `fill`, `map`, `filter`, `flat`, `flatMap`, `concat`, `slice`, `splice`, `sort`, `reverse`, `with`, `toSorted`, `toReversed`, `toSpliced`, `forEach`, `every`, `some`, `reduce`, `reduceRight`, `indexOf`, `lastIndexOf`, `includes`, `find*`, `copyWithin`, `keys`/`values`/`entries` consumers; `Array.from` | `this.length` (or source length) ≤ 2^24 and result slots × 16 ≤ callCap; `flat`/`flatMap`: depth ≤ 256 and a Go pre-count of produced elements stopping at the cap | fill killed at 975 MB, from 421 MB, map/sort 383 MB, forEach 2^31 never returns, flat DAG |
| G4 | `ArrayBuffer` (incl. `maxByteLength` option), `ArrayBuffer.prototype.slice`/`resize`, every typed array constructor incl. `Float16Array`, `%TypedArray%.from`/`of`, `%TypedArray%.prototype.slice`/`map`/`filter` (`subarray` allocates nothing: not wrapped) | byte length ≤ callCap | Float64Array 256 MB |
| G5 | `Function.prototype.apply`, `Reflect.apply`, `Reflect.construct` | array-like `length` ≤ 65,536 | apply/fromCharCode 383-415 MB |
| G6 | `JSON.parse` | Go pre-scan: text bytes × 24 ≤ callCap (`memory limit:`); nesting ≤ 256, else `SyntaxError: JSON nesting deeper than 256` (`KindRuntime`) | parse 607 MB, deep parse stack overflow |
| G7 | `JSON.stringify` | runs the original with a Go counting replacer composed over the caller's (function: call it, then count; array allow list: emulated); cap = callCap; `space` counted per line | stringify DAG 374 MB / 9 s (probe with replacer: aborts in 39 ms) |
| G8 | `BigInt.asUintN`, `BigInt.asIntN` | bits ≤ min(2^30, callCap × 8) | `asUintN(2**40)` fatal OOM |
| G9 | `String.prototype.split` | `this.length` × 64 bytes per piece estimate when separator is `''`, else no check | split 195 MB |
| G10 | RegExp (all methods) | not wrapped: `regexp2.DefaultMatchTimeout = Timeout` in the worker; timeout surfaces as catchable `RangeError: match timeout` | catastrophic regexp never interrupted |

Not guardable (operators and syntax, no hook): string `+` and template literals building ropes and
their flatten (`===`, `<`, template, property key); BigInt `**`, `*`, `<<` on huge values (goja
caps only `<<` at 2^30 bits); array spread and destructuring of sparse arrays; bound-function
chains (probe: a 300,000-deep `bind` chain passed the 1 GB probe watchdog); native recursion in
built-ins outside the list. A 300,000-deep Proxy chain ran fine (411 ms). Ceilings handle them: watchdog interrupt for
accumulation, hard exit for one-shot allocation, Go stack cap for recursion, parent kill for time.
They end as `KindMemory`/`KindStack`/`KindTimeout`, without position when the worker died.

Implementer probes each guard in `limits_test.go` (table below) with sizes just over the cap and
just under it (a legit call passes).

### Deadline, interrupt, cancel

- One deadline computed at `Exec` start (spawn time counts). Worker gets `Timeout − elapsed` and
  arms `time.AfterFunc(remaining, vm.Interrupt(interruptTimeout))`. goja's `Interrupt` stays set
  until a run takes it; the worker runs one script and exits, so `ClearInterrupt` is never needed.
- Cancel: parent kills the worker on ctx done (`KindCanceled`). No cooperative cancel message:
  kill is immediate and the worker holds nothing worth a graceful stop.
- Hard return: parent kills at deadline + 1 s grace (`KindTimeout`). Semaphore acquire honours ctx
  (`KindCanceled`).
- Any panic in the parent's Exec goroutine or in a `HostFunc` is recovered: `KindInternal` or a
  script-visible "internal error" respectively; one `slog.Error`, static message, `err` key,
  `scope: "jsengine"`. Panics inside the worker end the worker (`KindInternal`).

### JSON and big integers (question e)

- Input bindings, host-call returns and `kira.parseJSON` text become goja values in Go: a
  `json.Decoder` with `UseNumber` in token mode builds objects (`NewObject`, `Set` in source key
  order) and arrays. An integer literal (no `.`, `e`, `E`) inside ±(2^53 − 1) becomes a number;
  outside, `r.ToValue(*big.Int)`, which is a goja BigInt (probe: `typeof` `bigint`, exact digits,
  `> 5` works, `+ 1` throws TypeError). No marker on input.
- Script-side `JSON.parse` stays standard and lossy above 2^53 (probe: `18446744073709551617`
  parses to `18446744073709552000`). ARCHITECTURE says to use `kira.parseJSON` for nested JSON
  text.
- Decimals and exponents stay `number` (float64; `1e400` is `Infinity`, which encodes as `null`).
  Big decimals as exact values are not supported; P680 decides how SQL `numeric` arrives.
- Output: worker sets the encoding flag, calls the captured `JSON.stringify(value, countingReplacer)`
  with cap `OutputBytes`, clears the flag in `finally`. Bigints arrive as marker strings (sandbox
  item 5). A cycle, a throwing `toJSON` or the cap → `KindOutput`. Then a Go token rewrite turns
  marker strings back into bare integer literals (order kept, compact). So big integers from the
  input reach the AI as exact JSON numbers unless the script stringifies them. Probe: replacer adds
  about 3x to stringify time (3.5 MB: 101 ms plain, 294 ms counted).
- Marker: `\u0000` + 32 hex chars from 16 random bytes per run. If any input text contains it,
  draw again (bounded retries, then `KindInternal`).
- Key order: goja orders integer-like keys first, as ECMA-262 does (probe: `{"b":1,"2":2,"a":3,
  "1":4}` round-trips to `{"1":4,"2":2,"b":1,"a":3}`). ARCHITECTURE states it; `Result.JSON`
  documents "key order as JSON.stringify gives it".
- Strings: invalid UTF-8 in input becomes U+FFFD at decode; lone surrogates in output become U+FFFD
  in the Go rewrite. Output bytes are valid UTF-8.

### Source integrity and hash

- `SourceHash(source)`: lowercase hex SHA-256 of the exact bytes, no normalisation (CRLF stays):
  the approval card shows verbatim source and P676 binds approval to this hash the way
  `scriptruns` binds `Preview.Hash`.
- Validation in `Check` and `Exec`, `KindSource`: empty or blank; over 64 KiB; invalid UTF-8; NUL;
  bidirectional control characters U+202A to U+202E and U+2066 to U+2069 anywhere (Trojan Source).
  Error names the line and column of the first offending character.
- `Check`: validation, then parse and `CompileAST` in-process (no worker, no semaphore, never
  executes). Safe in-process: goja's parser caps nesting (probe: 65,000 `(`, `[`, `{`, `a=>`, `-`
  all stop at "Maximum nesting depth exceeded" in 2-32 ms, 8-16 MB of stack). Returns nil or
  `*Error` (`KindSyntax` with line and column, or `KindSource`).

### Errors

```go
type Kind string // syntax, runtime, timeout, canceled, memory, stack, source, input, output, internal

type Error struct {
	Kind    Kind    `json:"kind"`
	Message string  `json:"message"`          // capped at 2 KiB, "TypeError: ..." form for runtime
	Line    int     `json:"line,omitempty"`   // 1-based in the user's source; 0 when unknown
	Column  int     `json:"column,omitempty"` // 1-based
	Stack   []Frame `json:"stack,omitempty"`  // user frames only, at most 10
}
type Frame struct {
	Function string `json:"function,omitempty"`
	Line     int    `json:"line"`
	Column   int    `json:"column"`
}
func (e *Error) Error() string // "script <kind> error at line L, column C: <message>"
```

- `*goja.CompilerSyntaxError` → `KindSyntax`, position from `File.Position(Offset)` minus the
  wrapper line (probe: "Unexpected token ; at script:3:9" for user line 2); a position past the
  source clamps to the last line. Message without goja's " at …" suffix.
- `*goja.Exception` → `KindRuntime`. Message: error object `name: message`, or `String(value)` for a
  non-error throw (`throw null` gives "Uncaught null"). Frames from `Exception.Stack()`
  (`FuncName()`, `Position()`): drop native frames, frames named `__kira_*`, frames whose line is
  outside the user's source; subtract 1 from the line. `Line`/`Column` are the top user frame.
  A guard error identified by run state → `KindMemory`, same position rules.
- `*goja.InterruptedError` → value `interruptTimeout` gives `KindTimeout`, `interruptMemory` gives
  `KindMemory`; position from its stack (`at <eval>:L:C(pc)`; exported accessor if goja has one,
  else parse `String()`).
- `*goja.StackOverflowError` → `KindStack`.
- Worker exits: mapping above, no position.
- Scrub: source name is always the fixed `script`, so no host path appears. Go errors from host
  funcs reach the script as their `err.Error()`; callers own its text. Panic text never reaches the
  script or the agent ("internal error").
- Messages may echo data the script handled. The engine knows no secrets; P676 and P679 mask error
  text like any agent-bound text. Write that into ARCHITECTURE.
- The engine logs nothing about scripts or data; internal faults only, per `sloglint` rules
  (static message, `err` key, `scope: "jsengine"`).

## Tests

Package tests only, `apps/kira-space/internal/jsengine/*_test.go`, standard `testing`,
table-driven, `t.Parallel()` where the semaphore allows. `TestMain` dispatches `js-worker` to
`RunWorker`; tests use `newEngine` pointing at `os.Args[0]`. No flow test and no UI spec in P675:
the engine has no IPC surface; P676 (first feature) owns the split flow test plus UI spec. Each file
guards something hard to get right (limits, sandbox escape, token conversion with interacting rules,
frame mapping, process exit mapping); no CRUD or trivial-wrapper tests, no test of `SourceHash`
alone. Memory tests use `Limits.MemoryBytes` of 64 MiB so a hard exit happens well under the
container's memory; no test allocates above 512 MB in a child.

1. `limits_test.go`: infinite loop gives `KindTimeout` with position within timeout + 100 ms; a
   binding whose `HostFunc` blocks on a channel past the deadline gives `KindTimeout` by
   deadline + grace, the worker is killed and the slot released; ctx cancel mid-run gives
   `KindCanceled` and the child is gone (`Proc.Done`); push loop gives positioned `KindMemory`;
   garbage churn for 1.5 s does not trip memory; rope 2^29 `===` and `2n**(2n**30n)` give
   `KindMemory` (hard exit) and the parent heap (`runtime/metrics` heap objects delta) stays under
   16 MB; `BigInt.asUintN(2**40,-1n)` gives positioned `KindMemory` (G8); `JSON.parse` of 300,000
   nested `[` gives positioned `KindRuntime` (G6 depth); `String(a)` with `a=[a]` 300,000 deep
   gives positioned `KindMemory` (G2 depth); recursion gives `KindStack`
   (`StackOverflowError`); catastrophic regexp gives a catchable `RangeError` and, uncaught,
   `KindRuntime` before the deadline; each guard G1-G9 over cap gives positioned `KindMemory`, and
   the same call under cap succeeds; output over cap gives `KindOutput`; input over cap gives
   `KindInput` before spawn; input × 24 over `MemoryBytes` gives `KindInput`; the fifth concurrent
   Exec waits until a slot's worker exits; semaphore wait honours ctx; deadline spans spawn plus run.
2. `sandbox_test.go`: `typeof` list above is `undefined`; dynamic-code paths throw `EvalError`;
   `import('os')` is a syntax error; `//# sourceMappingURL=<temp file>` in a script never reads it
   (temp file with unique content; the run neither fails on it nor exposes it; plus a direct check
   that the parse option is set); `Object.prototype.x = 1`, `Math.random = …`, `JSON.parse = …`,
   `globalThis.y = 1`, redefining a binding all throw; wrapper break-out gains nothing;
   `Date.now()` and `new Date()` equal `Run.Now`; with `t.Setenv("TZ", "America/New_York")` in the
   parent (not parallel) `getTimezoneOffset() === 0` and `getHours() === getUTCHours()`;
   `Math.random` sequence equal across two runs with the same seed, different with another; the
   worker sees no parent environment variable (set one in the test, read nothing back through any
   global); Promise return gives `KindOutput`.
3. `json_test.go`: table over inputs 2^53 − 1 (number), 2^53 + 1, −2^63, 2^64, a 40-digit integer
   (bigint, exact out), `1.5`, `1e3`, `1e400`, negative zero, nested arrays and objects, key order
   with integer-like keys (pins integer-first order), duplicate keys, depth 256 passes and 257 fails
   `KindInput`; host-call round trip of a big integer through `HostFunc`; `kira.parseJSON`
   lossless; script `JSON.stringify(2n**64n)` gives a string; a string equal to `"\u0000"` plus 32
   hex chars that is not the run's marker stays a string; cycle in output gives `KindOutput`; host
   func error text reaches the script as an `Error` it can catch; host func panic gives "internal
   error" and the run continues; 10,001st host call throws; G7 composes with a user replacer
   function and an array allow list (same output as plain `JSON.stringify` under cap).
4. `errors_test.go`: syntax error on line 1, a middle line and the last line (unterminated brace)
   with exact line and column, same from `Check` and `Exec`; runtime error inside a nested user
   function gives user frames only with mapped lines, no `__kira_` frame; after an error inside
   `kira.parseJSON` the top frame is the user call site; message cap 2 KiB; `Check` refuses NUL,
   invalid UTF-8, U+202E and U+2067 with position, over 64 KiB, blank; `Check` never executes (a
   body that would loop forever passes `Check` instantly); `Error()` string shape; worker exit
   codes and stderr headers map to kinds (table over a fake command: `sh -c 'exit 75'`, a script
   printing `fatal error: runtime: out of memory` to stderr, `goroutine stack exceeds`, plain
   exit 1).

Run once near phase end: `go test ./apps/kira-space/internal/jsengine/ -count=1 -race`. Do not run
other suites (concurrent jobs share this machine). Also `go vet`, the repo's golangci-lint on the
package and `appwire`, and `GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build
./apps/kira-space/internal/jsengine/`. Timing assertions use generous margins (timeout 300 ms,
grace bound 1.5 s) and no sleep-based waits for state (channels only).

   as the first import, or `go mod tidy` drops the requirement), `engine.go`, `worker.go`,
   `watchdog.go`, `limits.go`, `source.go`, `sandbox.go`, `errors.go`, `protocol.go`, `freeze.js`,
   `appwire/wire.go`.
2. `feat(jsengine): size guards, lossless big integers and host bindings` — `guards.go`, `json.go`,
   `bindings.go`.
3. `test(jsengine): limits, sandbox, big-number and error tests` — four test files, plus any fixes
   they force (fixes as follow-up `fix(jsengine):` commits if found after commit 3).
4. `docs: P675 JS engine architecture and notices` — ARCHITECTURE, NOTICES, SPEC row and Result.

Every commit passes the pre-commit hook without `--no-verify`.

## Risks

- One main maintainer upstream. Mitigation: nothing outside the package names goja; the
  `Run`/`HostFunc` interface is engine-neutral and process-neutral.
- Guards are a hand-written list over goja's built-in surface; a goja upgrade can add an allocating
  built-in. The worker ceilings catch it (no app impact); a guard only improves the error. Upgrade
  checklist line in ARCHITECTURE: re-run `limits_test.go` and diff goja's `builtin_*.go` exports.
- Spawn cost per run on macOS unknown until measured (Result); a warm spare is the follow-up if
  over 100 ms.
- Worker re-exec on macOS reuses the signed app binary, as `memory-embed` already does; no new
  entitlement.
- Wall clock, not CPU: a loaded machine gives a script less work per second. Acceptable; limits are
  safety rails, not quotas.
- Sandbox hardening is Go-level over goja's intrinsics. A missed dynamic-code path would break the
  "user saw the code" rule, not isolation (same process sandbox, no fs, no network); sandbox tests
  enumerate the known paths.
- UTC-only local time can surprise a script expecting local time. P676 tool text says so.
- MPL-2.0 provenance of goja `ftoa` (Licences): user decision before commit 1.
